headline: Bangladesh signs 15-year deal with DP World to operate NCT
summary: The agreement was signed amid intense protests from port labour organisations and leftist groups who claim the deal threatens national sovereignty.
details: Bangladesh has signed a 15-year concession agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate the New Mooreing Container Terminal (NCT) at Chattogram port.
The deal was signed on Thursday afternoon at the Invest Bangladesh Auditorium, despite widespread opposition from various stakeholders.
Protests erupted in front of the auditorium and at the Chattogram port, leading to clashes between demonstrators and police, who eventually dispersed the crowd.
The Port Protection Committee and various labour organisations have announced a mass hunger strike starting Monday, October 12, to protest the deal.
Protesters argue that handing over the NCT to a foreign operator threatens the security and sovereignty of the country's primary port.
They have termed the deal 'suicidal' and demanded a reconsideration of the decision, claiming that the terms of the agreement were kept secret from the public.
The government has moved forward with the agreement to enhance port efficiency and operational capacity through international expertise.
caption:
A 15-year deal to operate the New Mooreing Container Terminal has been signed, but not without a clash.

Bangladesh has signed a 15-year concession agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate the New Mooreing Container Terminal (NCT) at Chattogram port.

The deal was signed on Thursday afternoon at the Invest Bangladesh Auditorium, despite widespread opposition from various stakeholders.

Protests erupted in front of the auditorium and at the Chattogram port, leading to clashes between demonstrators and police, who eventually dispersed the crowd.

The Port Protection Committee and various labour organisations have announced a mass hunger strike starting Monday, October 12, to protest the deal.

Protesters argue that handing over the NCT to a foreign operator threatens the security and sovereignty of the country's primary port.

They have termed the deal 'suicidal' and demanded a reconsideration of the decision, claiming that the terms of the agreement were kept secret from the public.

The government has moved forward with the agreement to enhance port efficiency and operational capacity through international expertise.

headline_marked: Rooppur Unit 1 [[approved to begin nuclear reaction]]
headline: Rooppur Unit 1 approved to begin nuclear reaction
summary: Bangladesh is set to become the 33rd country in the world to generate nuclear power as the first reactor is cleared for criticality.
details: The Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) has approved the start of a controlled chain reaction at the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant in Pabna's Ishurdi.
This approval moves the unit from a static phase into active operation, opening the possibility of trial electricity supply to the national grid by late December.
BAERA Chairman Mahmudul Hasan stated that two more regulatory approvals are required before the unit can formally supply power to the grid.
The process was previously delayed by technical complications with automatic pressure-relief safety valves, which were later resolved by a team of Russian specialists.
With first criticality, the reactor will begin its first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear fission chain reaction, followed by a power start-up phase.
The reactor's thermal power will initially rise to 3 percent and gradually increase to 20-30 percent before the generator is synchronised with the national grid.
Project officials expect trial production at varying power levels to continue for seven to eight months after grid connection.
Once operational, Bangladesh will join an exclusive group as the 33rd country in the world to generate nuclear power.
The project's original deadline of December 2025 has been extended twice to June 2028, with costs rising to Tk 1.39 trillion due to exchange-rate changes.
caption:
Bangladesh is one step closer to nuclear power. The first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has been approved for its first nuclear reaction.

The Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) has approved the start of a controlled chain reaction at the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant in Pabna's Ishurdi.

This approval moves the unit from a static phase into active operation, opening the possibility of trial electricity supply to the national grid by late December.

BAERA Chairman Mahmudul Hasan stated that two more regulatory approvals are required before the unit can formally supply power to the grid.

The process was previously delayed by technical complications with automatic pressure-relief safety valves, which were later resolved by a team of Russian specialists.

With first criticality, the reactor will begin its first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear fission chain reaction, followed by a power start-up phase.

The reactor's thermal power will initially rise to 3 percent and gradually increase to 20-30 percent before the generator is synchronised with the national grid.

Project officials expect trial production at varying power levels to continue for seven to eight months after grid connection.

Once operational, Bangladesh will join an exclusive group as the 33rd country in the world to generate nuclear power.

The project's original deadline of December 2025 has been extended twice to June 2028, with costs rising to Tk 1.39 trillion due to exchange-rate changes.
